# Frontline intake, interview 1

SYNTHETIC training material. No real people, interviews or customer data.
Scenario date: 2026-09-09. Evidence type: attributed simulated interview.

I receive requests in the intake queue. I copy tenant, request ID, customer ID and urgency into an email to operations. A normal request goes through a credit check and then fulfillment. I have seen urgent requests handled differently, but I do not know who owns those exceptions. My part ends when operations takes the request. I cannot speak for the whole process or name the overall process owner. We lose time chasing status. These are my recollections, not an observed process test.

examples/order-triage/inputs/03-operations.md
# Operations lead and workflow owner, interview 3

SYNTHETIC training material. No real people, interviews or customer data.
Scenario date: 2026-09-09. Evidence type: attributed simulated interview.

I own the bounded workflow from intake acceptance to recorded routing disposition. Current policy in this synthetic scenario, effective 2026-09-01: frontline sends the request to operations; operations triages urgency. Urgent requests go to the service desk for manual review and stop there with a disposition. Standard requests go to finance for the latest credit decision. Approved requests go to fulfillment; denied or missing decisions stay in finance review. Finance does not own urgent exceptions. The boundary ends at the routing disposition, before shipment or financial authorization. I confirmed this by walking all four fixture requests with the participants. The service desk operates across the internal/support boundary; fulfillment is a separate internal system.

# Finance analyst, interview 4

SYNTHETIC training material. No real people, interviews or customer data.
Scenario date: 2026-09-09. Evidence type: attributed simulated interview.

Credit approvals are events, not one row per request. Use the newest decision_seq within tenant and request_id. A previous denial may later be approved. Missing or denied latest decisions route standard requests to finance review. Finance does not assess urgent requests in this workflow. These statements were checked against the supplied synthetic approval rows together with operations.

# Data engineer, interview 5

SYNTHETIC training material. No real people, interviews or customer data.
Scenario date: 2026-09-09. Evidence type: attributed simulated interview.

The supplied SQLite setup represents four exports: intake.requests, crm.customers, finance.approvals and operations.handoffs. Requests have one row per (tenant, request_id). Customer identity is (tenant, customer_id), not customer_id alone. Approvals have one row per (tenant, request_id, decision_seq). Handoffs have one row per (tenant, request_id, event_seq). Only the most recent approval and handoff should enrich a request. There are four requests across north and south tenants. The schema and rows are synthetic, checked exports for this exercise.

examples/order-triage/inputs/07-security.md
# Security reviewer, interview 7

SYNTHETIC training material. No real people, interviews or customer data.
Scenario date: 2026-09-09. Evidence type: attributed simulated interview.

Tenant isolation is mandatory: a request must never be enriched with another tenant's customer. Retain the tenant key at each join and in outputs. The only authorized actions in this exercise are reading supplied synthetic files, running local SQLite/Python, and creating local project artifacts and simulated releases. No production credentials, live customer data, network database access, shipment, or financial mutation is authorized. A real deployment needs its own runtime authorization and controls.

# Reliability reviewer, interview 9

SYNTHETIC training material. No real people, interviews or customer data.
Scenario date: 2026-09-09. Evidence type: attributed simulated interview.

Rehearse loss of approval input using a local in-memory fault. Detect the routing failure, open an incident, record diagnosis and authorized repair, then run the same acceptance check again. An unsuccessful recovery attempt must keep the incident open. Restoring the original fixture input is within this exercise's authority. Do not weaken acceptance criteria or treat old passing evidence as a new test. Keep a follow-up to investigate feed availability before real deployment.

examples/order-triage/inputs/10-sponsor.md
# Sponsor and acceptance owner, interview 10

SYNTHETIC training material. No real people, interviews or customer data.
Scenario date: 2026-09-09. Evidence type: attributed simulated interview.

Bounded exercise: accept a synthetic request and produce one routing disposition; do not ship or approve credit. Operations owns it. Acceptance criteria: exactly one output per supplied (tenant, request_id), no customer data crossing tenant boundaries, and the expected routing dispositions. In this fixture north R1 standard/approved routes fulfillment; north R2 standard/denied routes finance-review; north R3 urgent routes service-desk; south R4 standard/approved routes fulfillment. Requirements should keep these three criteria separate. Verification is valid for this fixed fixture, not an unobserved real operation. Record remaining deployment work explicitly.
